For the Pythagoreans, number is the structure of reality: musical harmonies are whole-number ratios (2:1 octave, 3:2 fifth, 4:3 fourth), and the cosmos itself is ordered like music. Their community was a way of life with strict rules. The discovery that the diagonal of a square cannot be written as a ratio of whole numbers (irrational numbers) was a shock; tradition links it to Hippasos.
